title: A 64Gb/s/wire 10.5Tb/s/mm/Layer Single-Ended Simultaneous Bi-Directional Transceiver with Echo and Crosstalk Cancellation for a Die-to-Die Interface in 28nm CMOS
problem: Die-to-die (chiplet) interfaces demand ultra-high edge density and low BER; simultaneous bi-directional (SBD) signaling doubles data rate but introduces echo (near-end reflection) and crosstalk (NEXT/FEXT). Existing echo-cancellation circuits are power-hungry; removing ground shielding for density gains increases crosstalk vulnerability.
motivation: AI and HPC chiplet systems require 100+ Tb/s total die-to-die bandwidth in minimal footprint; removing ground shields doubles edge density but echo + NEXT + FEXT become problematic. Digital signal equalization adds latency/power; analog cancellation is tightly power-budgeted.
method: Single-ended SBD transceiver with integrated analog echo cancellation (EC), near-end crosstalk (NEXT), and far-end crosstalk (FEXT) cancellation. Shield-less channel design (ground shielding removed). Three-layer cancellation approach: EC suppresses echo from local transmitter; NEXT/FEXT cancellation handles coupling from aggressor wires on same die.
key_novelty: Combined echo + NEXT + FEXT cancellation in single transceiver for shield-less SBD die-to-die signaling.
contributions: 64Gb/s per-wire single-ended SBD signaling (128Gb/s effective with dual direction)
Echo cancellation reducing local TX reflection
NEXT cancellation (vs. prior art focusing only on FEXT)
FEXT cancellation for distant aggressor coupling
baselines: Prior SBD with echo cancellation only (no NEXT cancellation)
limitations: Abstract does not provide transceiver power consumption, latency, or scaling to longer/shorter channel lengths. PVT corner effects on cancellation performance not discussed.
primary_theme: High-density shield-less die-to-die transceiver with multi-source cancellation
